4. The defendant No.1 contested the suit by filing written statement denying all material allegations as made in the plaint contending, inter alia, that the suit is not maintainable in its present form without declaration and has no cause of action. The suit is barred by limitation, bad for defect of parties and hotchpot. The case of plaintiff is false and fabricated. The defendants had been possessing the suit land. C.S. Khatian No.156 was correctly recorded in the name of Golam Ali Howlader and Abdul Aziz. Golam Ali died leaving behind five sons namely Abdul Haque, Abdul Khaleque, Abdul Mazid, Abdur Rahman and Rahim and two daughters Siddika Khatoon and Fatema Khatoon and accordingly the suit land was correctly recorded in their names. The heirs and successive heirs of Golam Ali were not made parties in this suit. 

 9. Mr. Abdur Rahman Howlader, the learned Counsel appearing on behalf of the petitioners taking us through the judgment and decree of the High Court Division dated 02.02.2011 passed in Civil Revision No.1556 of 2000, the materials on record contends that the High Court Division erred in law in totally misconceiving the case of the petitioners upon misreading and misconstruing the evidence and materials on record and thereby misdirected beyond the law and facts of the suit in passing the erroneous decision making the Rule absolute which commit-ted serious miscarriage of justice. The learned Counsel for the petitioners next contends that plaintiffs have not been able to prove their title in the suit land and the suit is not maintainable in its present form. The learned Counsel argues finally that the suit land is specific and all the necessary parties have not been impleaded as defendants in the suit and the documents have not been marked and exhibited according to the law and further the whole properties in the jote have not been brought into the hotchpot of the schedule land, thus the High Court Division erred in holding that simple suit for partition was not maintainable in the absence of consequential relief for which the impugned judgment and decree is not tenable in the eye of law.
